title: Quick check: Authentication and Authorization UI

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Authentication and Authorization UI”?
options: The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Login interfaces must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
questions.answer_key: Login interfaces must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Authentication and Authorization UI: Login interfaces must respect trust boundaries; authorization and secrets are not protected by client-side UI alone.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Login interfaces?
options: Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
questions.answer_key: Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Authentication and Authorization UI: Keep secret keys and authorization checks on a trusted server.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Authentication and Authorization UI” complete?
options: Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Authentication and Authorization UI: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
